name: Vee Finance leveraged-trade swap without a valid price bound
summary: Vee Finance's leverage proxy swapped borrowed funds through whatever Pangolin pair getPair returned, with no liquidity floor or independent price bound and a mis-scaled amountOutMin. The attacker seeded thin pairs, opened leveraged positions that swapped borrowed WETH.e, WBTC.e and USDT.e into them for dust, then bought the funds back out of its own pairs, leaving Vee with worthless positions.

campaign.selection: successful txs from any EOA to attacker contracts 0x255945a4f673851633355b2592f602025ca20142 or 0x490d25a327768bd5e3d2bf98b8e10419b3e70b82 calling 0x7cda23fa or 0xc66851a6 whose receipt shows a net Transfer outflow from a Vee market (comptroller 0x43aad7d8 getAllMarkets), excluding the anchor

notes: Reset: the proxy's switch back to implementation 0x8e03cf8a at block 4284011 made the exploited code active; the markets, collateral factors and oracle were configured before it.

Loss sums each campaign transaction's net token outflow from Vee's markets in receipt logs (loss.mjs ignores bundles), so concurrent user redemptions are excluded. WETH.e, WBTC.e and LINK.e use DefiLlama ETH, BTC and LINK prices at the anchor; USDT.e is at par.
The implementation is unverified; the mechanism is read from traces and Halborn's analysis.
